subjects.name: Basics of Electronics Engineering
subjects.objective: This subject provides an opportunity for the students to get familiarized with all basic electronics components and study the characteristics of diode, transistors etc. Also student will get the ability to do simulation of corresponding circuits. The lab is designed for second semester students. Credits Earned: 3 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able 1. Develop the conceptual knowledge about the semiconductor and learn fundaments of terminal characteristics of PN junction diode and design /analyze fundamental circuits based on PN junction diode. 2. Identify limitation of diode and learning fundaments of transistor structure, types and behavioral characteristics and comparison of various transistor configurations. 3. Exploring the DC load line, biasing methods, comparisons in various amplifier configurations by understanding effects of change in Q-point by factors affecting stability. 4. Understand the various configurations of feedback amplifier, fundamental of FET devices and MOSFET. 5. Understanding and awareness about various type of component like LED, LDR, Varactor Diode, Photo voltaic diode etc. 6. Able to get aware about various types of available cable and connectors.

firstHalfUnits.title: Semiconductor diode characteristics and its Applications 5.5

allSyllabusUnits.title: Semiconductor diode characteristics and its Applications 5.5
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Types of semiconductor.  P-N junction diode formation and characteristics.  Applications - Diode as rectifier, half wave, full wave and bridge rectifier.  Need of filters.  C, L, LC, π filters.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Transistor characteristics and biasing 10
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  PNP and NPN transistors, conduction through transistor leakage current, relationship between α and β.  Transistor configuration & characteristics for CB, CE, CC.  Load line and biasing methods of transistor.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Transistor as an amplifier: 2.5
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Common emitter amplifier.  Common collector amplifier  Multistage amplifier

allSyllabusUnits.title: Special purpose diode and Applications 5
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  JFET and MOSFET  Special purpose diode, Zener diode & it's application,  Photo diode  LDR  Photovoltaic Cell  Light Emitting Diode  Varactor Diode  Digital Display

allSyllabusUnits.title: Oscillators 4
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Working principle of oscillator  Different types of oscillators: Hartley oscillator, Colpitts oscillator, Phase- Shift Oscillator, Wien Bridge Oscillator, Crystal Oscillator, FET Oscillator.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Cables and Connectors 1.5
allSyllabusUnits.topics:  Cables: coaxial cable, twisted pair cable and fiber optic cable  Connectors: coaxial cable connectors, RJ-45, RS-232, HDMI connectors. Total 28.5 100 Syllabus for Diploma Engineering Information and Communication Technology

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Semiconductor diode characteristics and its Applications 5.5; Transistor characteristics and biasing 10.

subjects.name: Electronic Practice
subjects.objective: This subject of ‘Electronics Practice’ is focused to provide the students with more hands-on experience and also enable them to develop and test simple PCB circuits. Selection of components, wiring, soldering, disordering, testing and troubleshooting, are some of the basic skills required by industry from any electronics engineering diploma holder. Students also need to develop enough learning confidence to complete entire project work related to various courses in subsequent higher level semesters. Hence, this course is designed to develop these vital skills required by the electronic industry through various laboratory experiences and strategies like mini-projects. Credits Earned: ​2 Credits
course_outcomes: ​After completion of this course, student will be able to ● Identify a particular component from the given group of active & passive electronic components ● Use of CRO and Function Generator for various wave generation and measurements. ● Will be able to analyze and interprets IC manual available in market ● Student will be able identify various hardware components and devices like diode, transformer, relay, Bread board ICs etc.. ● Will able to do soldering and de-soldering of general purpose components. ● Will able to create small project and trouble shoot same project.

firstHalfUnits.title: Introduction to IC and SMD & Datasheet Interpretation : 6

allSyllabusUnits.title: Electronic Components: 4
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Passive components: ​Various type of resistors, inductors, capacitors, potentiometers, Thermistor, Transformer Active components: ​Characteristics of ​Diode, Zener diode, Varactor diode, LED, Photo diode, BJT​, ​Photo transistor, FET, LDR, Solar cell, Photocell, Optocoupler.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Various Sources & Measuring Instruments: 10
allSyllabusUnits.topics: AC & DC power supply, Various Voltage & Current source, Measuring Instrument ​CRO & DSO, Digital Multimeter (DMM), and Function Generator.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Cables, Connectors & Relays: 6
allSyllabusUnits.topics: General specifications of cables- characteristic impedance, current carrying capacity twin core cable twisted & shielded type, optical fiber cable General specifications of connectors- contact resistance, breakdown voltage, insulation resistance ,Constructional diagram, applications of BNC, D series, Audio, Video, printer, edge, FRC, RJ 45 connectors. Construction, working and application of general purpose relay, NO, NC contact, reed relays, solid state relays.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to IC and SMD & Datasheet Interpretation : 6
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of IC’s, monolithic IC, thick & thin film IC, hybrid IC, linear IC, digital IC Using data sheet understand the IC packages-SIP, TO 5 ,Flat , DIP, pin Identification, temperature ranges, device identification Compare various IC’s and SMD Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Electronic workshop tool : 12
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Bread board, Copper clad laminate sheet, Solder iron, solder-stand, solder-wire, flux, flexible wire, hookup wire, cables, fuses, Cutter, plier, screw-driver set, wire stripper, de-solder pump, De-solder wick, drilling machine

allSyllabusUnits.title: Sensor Interfacing : 15
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction of open sources boards IDE, basics of programming using IDE, IO Control using IDE, Interfacing of switch, LED, Various Sensors and Actuators. TOTAL HOURS 53 100

[8 marks] Analyze a realistic task involving Fundamental and Derived units in Applied Physics. Explain the governing principle, justify the method or decision, and include a verification check and limitation.
[8 marks] Analyze a realistic task involving MKS and SI in Applied Physics. Explain the governing principle, justify the method or decision, and include a verification check and limitation.
Answers:
Model answer (8 marks)

**Meaning/purpose (2 marks):** Newton's first law says an object remains at rest or moves uniformly in a straight line unless a non-zero resultant force acts. Inertia is resistance to changing motion.

**Principles/steps (3 marks):** Explain the concept in logical order and relate it to syllabus areas such as Newton's first law of motion; momentum; Newton’s second law of motion; conservation of momentum. State relevant components, formulas, assumptions or procedures.

**Application/example (2 marks):** Apply it to a concrete Applied Physics problem; identify the objective, selected method and expected outcome.

**Verification/conclusion (1 mark):** Check the outcome against the objective and mention a meaningful limitation, error source or trade-off.

Marking guide: meaning/purpose 2; principles/steps 3; application/example 2; verification/conclusion 1.

Model answer (8 marks)

**Meaning/purpose (2 marks):** Stress & strain along with their types is covered in “Properties of Matter”. A good answer should define its purpose, explain its main components or steps, connect it to Hooke's law and modulus of elasticity-Young, bulk and modulus of rigidity, Viscosity, newton's law of viscosity, provide a practical example and state how the result can be checked.

**Principles/steps (3 marks):** Explain the concept in logical order and relate it to syllabus areas such as Hooke's law and modulus of elasticity-Young; bulk and modulus of rigidity; Viscosity; newton's law of viscosity. State relevant components, formulas, assumptions or procedures.

**Application/example (2 marks):** Apply it to a concrete Applied Physics problem; identify the objective, selected method and expected outcome.

**Verification/conclusion (1 mark):** Check the outcome against the objective and mention a meaningful limitation, error source or trade-off.

Marking guide: meaning/purpose 2; principles/steps 3; application/example 2; verification/conclusion 1.

Model answer (8 marks)

**Meaning/purpose (2 marks):** A unit is a standard for expressing a physical quantity. Fundamental units are independent standards; derived units combine them. Convert values to compatible units before calculations.

**Principles/steps (3 marks):** Explain the concept in logical order and relate it to syllabus areas such as Definition of unit; systems of units- CGS; MKS and SI; introduction to accuracy. State relevant components, formulas, assumptions or procedures.

**Application/example (2 marks):** Apply it to a concrete Applied Physics problem; identify the objective, selected method and expected outcome.

**Verification/conclusion (1 mark):** Check the outcome against the objective and mention a meaningful limitation, error source or trade-off.

Marking guide: meaning/purpose 2; principles/steps 3; application/example 2; verification/conclusion 1.

Questions: [8 marks] Explain Number sets and laws of indices. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain HCF and LCM of integers. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain HCF and LCM of fractions and decimals. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Polynomial definitions and arithmetic operations. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
Number sets include natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, irrational numbers and real numbers, with each set having specific membership rules. For a non-zero base a, powers follow laws such as a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. These laws require attention to conditions such as non-zero denominators and the base not being zero for a^0. For example, 2^3 × 2^4 ÷ 2^5 = 2^(3+4−5) = 2^2 = 4.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
The HCF is the greatest positive integer that divides every given integer; the LCM is the smallest positive common multiple. Prime factorization is a reliable method: 12 = 2^2 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3^2. For HCF, take common prime factors with the smallest exponents, giving 2 × 3 = 6. For LCM, take each prime factor with the greatest exponent, giving 2^2 × 3^2 = 36. For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
First express fractions in their lowest terms. For positive fractions, the usual course rules are HCF = HCF of numerators divided by LCM of denominators, and LCM = LCM of numerators divided by HCF of denominators. Thus for 2/3 and 4/5, HCF = 2/15 and LCM = 4. For decimals, convert values to integers by multiplying by an appropriate power of ten, find the HCF/LCM, then rescale the result. Keep the decimal-place adjustment consistent and verify the resulting multiples or divisors.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A polynomial is an expression formed from constants and variables with non-negative integer exponents and coefficients. Like terms have the same variable part and exponents, so only their coefficients are combined. For example, (2x + 3) + (x − 5) = 3x − 2. The degree of a non-zero polynomial in one variable is the highest exponent with a non-zero coefficient; the degree of 3x^4 − 2x^2 + 7 is four. Keep signs and exponents unchanged while grouping terms, and simplify before identifying the degree.

An algebraic identity is an equality that holds for every permitted value of its variables. Common identities include (a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, (a−b)^2 = a^2 − 2ab + b^2, and (a+b)(a−b) = a^2 − b^2. The middle term in a squared binomial is important; omitting it or using the wrong sign is a common error. Substitution can check a result.

Perimeter measures the total distance around a plane figure; area measures the enclosed surface. For a rectangle, perimeter is 2(l+w) and area is lw. For a square, perimeter is 4a and area is a². For a triangle, area is ½ × base × perpendicular height; for a circle, circumference is 2πr and area is πr². Use compatible units, distinguish linear units from square units, and identify the required dimension rather than assuming a sloping side is the perpendicular height. State the formula, substitute values and report units.

[8 marks] Analyze a realistic problem involving polynomial definitions and arithmetic operations, such as simplifying (2x + 3) + (x − 5) and identifying degree. Present a reasoned approach, justify key decisions, and state an important limitation or verification check.
Answers:
Model answer:
Number sets include natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, irrational numbers and real numbers, with each set having specific membership rules. For a non-zero base a, powers follow laws such as a^m × a^n = a^(m+n), a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. These laws require attention to conditions such as non-zero denominators and the base not being zero for a^0. For example, 2^3 × 2^4 ÷ 2^5 = 2^(3+4−5) = 2^2 = 4.

Model answer:
The HCF is the greatest positive integer that divides every given integer; the LCM is the smallest positive common multiple. Prime factorization is a reliable method: 12 = 2^2 × 3 and 18 = 2 × 3^2. For HCF, take common prime factors with the smallest exponents, giving 2 × 3 = 6. For LCM, take each prime factor with the greatest exponent, giving 2^2 × 3^2 = 36. For positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the two integers.

Answers:
Model answer:
Classify numbers carefully: integers include negative whole-number values, rational numbers can be expressed as a ratio of integers with non-zero denominator, irrational values cannot be so expressed, and real numbers include rational and irrational values. For a non-zero base a, use a^m a^n = a^(m+n), a^m/a^n = a^(m−n), (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^0 = 1. State domain restrictions and simplify stepwise; exponents add when multiplying like bases and subtract when dividing them.

Model answer:
For integers, prime-factorize and use minimum exponents for HCF and maximum exponents for LCM. For positive fractions in lowest terms, use HCF(numerators)/LCM(denominators) for HCF, and LCM(numerators)/HCF(denominators) for LCM. For decimals, scale all values by the same power of ten to make integers, calculate HCF or LCM, then reverse the scale. Example: HCF(12,18)=6 and LCM(12,18)=36. Check that the HCF divides the original integers and the LCM is a common multiple.
